name: Alliances
description: A mechanic where players can form temporary or permanent pacts, treaties, or teams with other players. These alliances often involve sharing resources, coordinating strategies, non-aggression agreements, or working towards common goals. Alliances can be formal or informal, and the rules for forming, breaking, or betraying them are key aspects of the mechanic.

parameters.name: Formation Rules
parameters.description: How alliances are formed (e.g., mutual agreement, specific action, triggered by game state).

parameters.name: Benefits of Alliance
parameters.description: What advantages do allied players receive (e.g., shared victory conditions, resource sharing, defensive pacts, combined strength).

parameters.name: Breaking/Betrayal Rules
parameters.description: Conditions or consequences for breaking an alliance or betraying an ally.
parameters.default_value: No formal penalty, but potential in-game repercussions from other players.

parameters.name: Alliance Exclusivity/Size
parameters.description: Can a player be in multiple alliances? How many players can be in one alliance?
parameters.default_value: One alliance at a time, typically 2 players.

examples_in_games.specific_implementation_notes: Core to the game, alliances are informal, constantly shifting, and betrayal is expected.
Players can make deals, form alliances (often non-binding), and trade support for promissory notes.

examples_in_games.game_name: Dune / Rex: Final Days of an Empire
examples_in_games.specific_implementation_notes: Players can form formal alliances which allow them to combine forces and share victory conditions.
While not formal 'alliances' in all cases, factions often have to cooperate or make temporary deals to prevent a dominant player from winning, or some factions can form coalitions.

notes_on_combination_modification: Alliances introduce a strong social and psychological layer to games. The potential for trust and betrayal creates memorable moments. They work well in games with direct player conflict or shared threats. Modifications can include hidden alliances, rules for forced alliances, or different levels of alliance commitment.
